close_reason: Implemented verify_sct_for_precert with bit-exact bytes matching against pyca/cryptography oracle. Coverage: 21 unit tests (verify.rs incl. 2 bit-exact oracle assertions tbs_without_sct_list_matches_oracle_bytes + issuer_key_hash_matches_oracle_bytes) + 8 integration tests (tests/verify_precert.rs) + openssl cross-check on oracle SCT signature. All 4 acceptance criteria met. Oracle script gen_precert_entry_sct.py is self-validating (Python-side strip-extension DER walker asserts oracle bytes match what cryptography's CertificateBuilder produces without SCT-list).
description:
## Why

Pre-certs are the CT submission mechanism: a CA submits a cert with the "poison" extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.3, critical, value NULL) to a CT log; the log returns an SCT; the CA then issues the real cert with the SCT embedded and the poison extension removed.

The SCT's signed_struct uses entry_type = precert_entry (1), which has a different tbs_cert encoding: the poison extension must be STRIPPED before signing, and the issuer is replaced by issuer_key_hash. Without this, embedded SCTs in real-world certs won't verify.

Depends on parser (child .1) and signature verifier (child .3) — extends .3.

## What

**Pre-cert detection** (RFC 6962 §3.1):
- The cert contains the SCT extension (1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.2) — flagging the FINAL cert.
- A pre-cert (submission) contains the poison extension (1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.3) marked critical.

**TBS reconstruction for precert_entry** (RFC 6962 §3.2):

```
struct {
    opaque issuer_key_hash[32];     // SHA-256 of issuer's SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes
                                    // (the byte string of SPKI, hashed)
    TBSCertificate tbs_certificate; // DER of TBSCertificate with poison ext removed
} PreCert;
```

The TBSCertificate is the leaf's TBS DER, but with the SignedCertificateTimestampList extension REMOVED (since the log signed before it was added). For a real-world cert with embedded SCTs, we are reconstructing what the log saw at submission time.

Implementation:
1. Parse the cert's TBSCertificate.
2. Filter out the SCT-list extension (1.3.6.1.4.1.11129.2.4.2).
3. Re-encode TBSCertificate DER.
4. Compute SHA-256 of the ISSUER cert's SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes (issuer cert needed — caller supplies, or we walk a chain).
5. Concatenate issuer_key_hash || tbs_der into the signed_struct.

## Public API extension (on top of child .3)

```rust
impl<V: SignatureVerifier> SctVerifier<V> {
    /// Verify ONE SCT where entry_type = precert_entry.
    /// Caller supplies the issuer cert so we can hash its SPKI.
    pub fn verify_sct_for_precert(
        &self,
        sct: &SignedCertificateTimestamp,
        leaf_cert_der: &[u8],
        issuer_cert_der: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<&CtLog, Error>;
}
```

## Test fixtures + oracle

Real-world cert with embedded SCT + the issuer's cert. Oracle: pyca/cryptography's SCT verifier OR Chrome's CT enforcement (the cert validates in a CT-enforcing browser).

The trickiest part is bit-exact TBSCertificate re-encoding after extension removal. Test that the reconstructed TBSCertificate DER matches what pyca produces given the same inputs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `verify_sct_for_precert` validates a real-world embedded-SCT cert.
- [ ] Bit-exact TBSCertificate-without-poison re-encoding matches an independent oracle.
- [ ] If the leaf has no SCT list extension at all, the function returns an error indicating it shouldn't be called (not a pre-cert SCT scenario).
- [ ] At least one tampered-issuer test: wrong issuer_key_hash causes verification failure.

## Effort

~200 lines + tests. ~1 day. TBS re-encoding edge cases drive the work.

## Filed as

Child .4 of PKIX-baac per its recommended decomposition.
notes: Approach: Option A (parse-mutate-encode via x509-cert + der::Encode), same pattern pkix-path uses in verify_cert_signature (lib.rs:2742-2748). Validated x509-cert TBS re-encoding is bit-exact for signed-bytes preservation on real chains (pkix-path's chain validation depends on it). Will fall back to surgical byte-level edit only if a real-world fixture round-trip fails. Plan: (1) gen_precert_entry_sct.py oracle (mirrors gen_x509_entry_sct.py shape); (2) verify_sct_for_precert + helpers in src/verify.rs; (3) tests/verify_precert.rs integration tests; (4) lib.rs Limitations rustdoc update. Acceptance criterion 'bit-exact tbs-no-poison matches oracle' = Python writes expected-tbs-no-sct.bin, Rust test asserts byte-equality.
title: pkix-ct: pre-cert detection and poison-stripping for SCT verification
